record.paper_title: Basic kinetic wealth-exchange models: common features and open problems
record.context_brief: Analytic formula for generalized model parameter
record.original_question: In the generalized homogeneous C-model where each agent's exchanged wealth fraction is constrained to lie between lower and upper bounds equivalent to saving parameters λ and λ′ with λ < λ′ < 1, can one derive a simple analytical formula for the Gamma-distribution shape parameter n as a function of the two saving parameters λ and λ′, rather than determining n only from numerical simulation?

evidence.quote: However, we have not found a simple analytical formula for fitting the dependence of the parameter n on the saving parameters λ and λ′.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following kinetic wealth-exchange model with N agents. Each agent i holds a non-negative wealth x_i(t). At each discrete time step, two agents i and j are selected uniformly at random and perform a conservative trade

  x_i' = x_i - Δx,    x_j' = x_j + Δx,

where the exchanged amount Δx is determined as follows. Fix two real parameters 0 ≤ λ < λ' < 1 (the "saving" bounds). For each trade, let ε be drawn uniformly on [0,1] and define an effective exchange fraction μ that, conditioned on being applied symmetrically to both agents, corresponds to saving parameters constrained to lie in the interval [λ, λ']. Concretely, define

  Δx = (1 - λ_i) x_i - [ε (1 - λ_i) x_i + (1 - ε)(1 - λ_j) x_j]·(something making the exchange conservative),

with the constraint that the effective per-agent saving fractions remain bounded between λ and λ'. (Equivalently, this is the homogeneous "C-model" in which every agent's saving propensity is required to lie in [λ, λ'].)

It is known empirically that, in the stationary regime, the rescaled wealth distribution P(x) is well approximated by a Gamma density

  f_n(x) = (n^n / Γ(n)) x^{n-1} e^{-n x},   x > 0,

with mean 1 and shape parameter n = n(λ, λ') > 0 depending on the two saving bounds, and that in the degenerate case λ = λ' the formula n(λ) = (1 + 2λ)/(1 - λ) holds.

Problem: Derive a closed-form analytical expression for the Gamma shape parameter n as a function of the two saving bounds λ and λ' (with λ < λ' < 1), reducing in the limit λ' → λ to n(λ) = (1+2λ)/(1-λ), or prove that no such elementary closed form exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent surveys on kinetic exchange models for wealth distributions (e.g., reviews from 2007 and 2010) continue to report only the uniform-saving formula n(λ) = (1+2λ)/(1-λ) and treat the two-bound generalization numerically. No explicit closed-form expression for n(λ, λ') in the heterogeneous-bound C-model was located in the available literature, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Kinetic Exchange Models for Income and Wealth Distributions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses gamma-distribution fits in saving-propensity models; uniform-saving case yields n = (1+2λ)/(1-λ).
status_evidence.claim: Standard analytical result is known only for the single-parameter (uniform) saving case.

status_evidence.title: Wealth distribution: To be or not to be a Gamma?
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews gamma-distribution approximations in CC/CCM models; relies on numerical fitting of shape parameter for generalized cases.
status_evidence.claim: For generalizations beyond uniform saving, the shape parameter is typically determined numerically.

status_evidence.title: Gamma-distribution and Wealth inequality
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses gamma fits but does not provide closed form for two-bound generalized C-model.
status_evidence.claim: No analytical formula for n(λ, λ') is reported.
